label: copy-phase input token a (fed-back a, from the 2nd copied output onward)
explanation: Token feature for the letter a being fed back as input during the copy phase. All activation mass is at copy-phase steps where in_tok is a; it never fires on the original-phase a or at the delimiter step, and never on any other input token. Without the recall_idx condition: recall 1.0, precision 0.74. Requiring recall_idx >= 2 (that is, the fed-back a is original token 1 or later and not the first copied token) drops very weak activations when a is fed back at the first copy-phase input, giving dev F1 0.92 and mass recall 0.99. Strongest activations (about 0.9-1.0 of max) come when a is fed back as original token 1 (recall_idx 2). The second of two consecutive fed-back a tokens activates more weakly (about 0.3-0.6). The remaining false positives are fed-back a steps where the feature stays silent, mostly later in long sequences.

issues: The predicate and its main claims hold. On test, (phase==2)&(in_tok==a)&(recall_idx>=2) gives P 0.883, R 0.969, F1 0.924, mass recall 0.990, which matches the report. The profile confirms zero activations in the original and delimiter phases and on every input token other than a.

Two of the magnitude claims are false. (1) 'Strongest activations come at recall_idx 2' is wrong. Of the top-quartile activations, recall_idx==2 covers 0.17, recall_idx==3 covers 0.40 and recall_idx==4 covers 0.28. Precision is 0.877 at recall_idx 2, 0.978 at 3 and 0.958 at 4. recall_idx 2 activations sit in the middle of the range; the peak is at recall_idx 3-4, meaning a fed back as original token 2-3. recall_idx>=5 is weighted toward the bottom quartile (coverage 0.47 in the lowest quartile, 0.15 in the top).

(2) 'The second of two consecutive fed-back a tokens activates more weakly (0.3-0.6 of max)' is not supported. The prev_tok==a subset has precision 0.877, about the same as the base, and flat activation-quartile coverage (0.032, 0.033, 0.036, 0.030). It is no weaker than other a steps.

The roughly 12% false positives follow graded trends, not a clean class. Precision is 0.95 for L<=6 versus 0.82-0.87 for L 7-9, 0.80 at to_go==0, 0.79 at recall_idx>=5 and 0.80 at recall_idx==2 with L>=8. Excluding these subsets lowers test F1 (0.894 and 0.897 versus 0.924), so no better predicate exists along these lines.

The recall_idx>=2 refinement is justified. The recall_idx==1 a steps have precision 0.12 and hold only 0.9% of mass. The missed activations (1.0% of mass) are weak (about 0.02-0.2 of max) at the first fed-back a.
Recommendation: keep the label and predicate, but fix the explanation's magnitude claims.
